verdict.rationale: Keycloak is itself a standards-based OAuth 2.0/OIDC authorization server. Its docs cover a discovery (well-known) endpoint, dynamic client registration, token introspection for verifying tokens, revocation, client credentials and fine-grained authorization, which is the core of putting an OAuth flow in front of an MCP server. Nothing in the evidence documents MCP-specific use or compliance with the MCP authorization spec, so the 'spec-compliant for MCP' part rests on general OAuth support only. Missing for 10: MCP-specific documentation or guide, evidence of PKCE / resource indicators / protected-resource metadata support, explicit token scope configuration, independent hands-on corroboration with remote agents.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can put a spec-compliant OAuth authorization flow in front of my MCP server so remote agents connect with scoped, verifiable tokens

citations.quote: Keycloak is based on standard protocols and provides support for OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0, and SAML.
The dynamic client registration endpoint is used to dynamically register clients.
The introspection endpoint is used to retrieve the active state of a token. In other words, you can use it to validate an access or refresh token.
It lists endpoints and other configuration options relevant to the OpenID Connect implementation in Keycloak.
Client Credentials are used when clients (applications and services) want to obtain access on behalf of themselves rather than on behalf of a user.
